comment.comment:
I've been holding $MASK for weeks now and every day of this stretch closed above $4.2M. Consistent, every day lol

From Oct 27 to Nov 3 it did ~$37M in volume (~$4.6M a day), $131.4M since Oct 1, ~$183K in platform fees this stretch and $658.5K in total.

On top of that $331K got bought back and burned across 7 buybacks, 3.65% of the total supply is gone, and 1,728 ZEC (~$2.3M) went out to $MASK holders.

If you're new, NullMask is pretty much a privacy pool that runs inside the wallet you already use. You deposit, withdraw to a fresh address, and zero-knowledge proofs break the direct link between the two. Every deposit gets screened first, so flagged funds get refused.

Zcash keeps its privacy on its own chain, NullMask just went live on Avalanche as chain #6 next to Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain and Solana, with Monad and Arbitrum next.

They also shipped NullMask Pay, where you send a link and get paid straight into your private balance, NullMask Exchange powered by PancakeSwap, and a Beldex partnership that brings shielded transfers and swaps to BDX on BNB Chain.

Points Season One is already at 20K+ wallets with a counted withdrawal and $46.3M in withdrawals earning points, and now holding earns too, 1 point per $100 per day on your pool balance.

As if that wasn't enough, the team keeps showing up on air, Privacy Is Back Ep 5 with Avalanche and Spectre AI, Ep 6 with Monad and Zebec, plus MCG and Balance's Market Manifesto Ep 28.

Still so early on this one imo

comment.comment:
$ORBIO | The Cost of Privacy. And the Value of Trust. 🪐

I've just shared my thoughts on @0x_aster's latest article, The Cost of Privacy.

And I believe it reveals something important about where @orbiodotso is heading.

For months, we've been watching Orbio evolve from an AI credit marketplace into a broader inference infrastructure platform.

Now the team is exploring a potentially more defensible business model.

Not just selling AI cheaper. Building AI that people can actually trust.

Yash's article goes beyond marketing promises. It examines encryption, secure enclaves, hardware verification, and the limitations that still exist.

What caught my attention is the willingness to acknowledge those limitations.

Because privacy shouldn't depend entirely on someone saying, "Trust us."

It should become increasingly verifiable.

And if Orbio can make that protection accessible without sacrificing usability, it could have something genuinely valuable.

But as an investor, I still want to see the next step:
• Users choosing Orbio for its privacy
• Recurring payments beyond free credits
• Sustainable infrastructure economics
• Clear value creation for $ORBIO holders

The technology is becoming more ambitious. Now the business needs to prove itself.

I continue holding $ORBIO, and the long-term thesis remains alive.

I published my full perspective on X, including why I think trust could become more valuable than competing on discounts.

👇 Read my quote-post:
https://x.com/Vlad007T/status/2118609748119474605

A discount can be copied. Trust has to be earned. 🪐
